outline.rationale: The user is a complete database beginner aiming to build an app backend, so the outline starts from zero (install/connect, what tables are) and builds toward backend-specific practical skills. Nodes 1-3 establish fundamentals a newcomer cannot skip: getting Postgres running, understanding the relational model, and reading/writing data with SQL. Node 4 (schema design) and 5 (constraints/transactions) cover data modeling and consistency, both explicitly called out as backend priorities. Node 6 (connecting from code) is the core "wiring Postgres into an app" skill and is essential for a backend developer but irrelevant to a pure SQL learner. Node 7 (indexes) is included at a beginner-practical level because slow queries are a real backend pain point, but kept narrow rather than deep tuning theory. Node 8 (migrations) addresses schema evolution, which any real app backend needs. I deliberately excluded DBA/ops topics (replication, backups at scale, performance tuning internals) per the confirmed scope, and avoided history/theory filler. Nodes are MECE: setup, model concepts, querying, design, integrity, integration, performance, and change management have low content overlap.
